blocks.text: iOS 26 opened Apple’s 26 naming cycle with a new visual system and wider personalization across the Lock Screen, Home Screen, core apps, and media. Its communication and assistance work included translation, unfamiliar-caller handling, visual search, and richer CarPlay and Wallet experiences.
Apple Intelligence capabilities vary by device, language, and region, so individual feature availability should be checked against Apple’s current requirements.

iPadOS 26 paired Apple’s new design with a major multitasking redesign built around resizable windows, familiar controls, tiling, Exposé, and a menu bar. Files, background tasks, local recording, Preview, Journal, and Phone expanded the iPad’s productivity range.
Apple Intelligence features remain subject to supported hardware, languages, and regions; their presence in the version does not imply availability on every compatible iPad.

macOS Tahoe 26 introduced Liquid Glass and broader personalization for folders, icons, widgets, Control Center, and the menu bar. Spotlight, Shortcuts, translated communication, the Phone app, and iPhone Live Activities concentrated the release on faster everyday workflows and Continuity.
Intelligent automation and translation depend on supported hardware, languages, and regions; Apple’s live documentation remains the authority for current availability.
tvOS 26 was a shared-room release that paired Liquid Glass and a more cinematic TV app with Music Sing, FaceTime, profiles, and AirPlay improvements.
The visual treatment depends on supported Apple TV 4K models, and using an iPhone as a Music Sing microphone requires compatible devices.
visionOS 26 made spatial content more persistent through widgets, scenes, and spatial web experiences while advancing Personas, shared experiences, immersive media, accessibility, and enterprise use.
Some spatial and immersive experiences require particular hardware, compatible content, or regional availability; the archive records the documented release rather than promising universal access.
watchOS 26 combined Apple’s new design with more health interpretation and proactive assistance, including hypertension notifications, Sleep Score, Workout Buddy, and Smart Stack hints.

Hypertension notifications are not a diagnosis and have age, hardware, region, and regulatory limits. Workout Buddy also depends on supported hardware and language settings, with a nearby iPhone required in some configurations.

blocks.text: iOS 26.4 was a substantial spring update centered on Apple Music discovery and creation, accessibility controls, AirPods Max 2 support, productivity improvements, and a stronger default security posture for newly configured devices.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately 13 topic areas and 17 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change as Apple revises the page.
iPadOS 26.4 combined new Music and creative tools with accessibility controls, multitasking refinements, and Safari changes intended to make window state easier to understand.
The shared iOS and iPadOS developer notes contained approximately 13 topic areas and 17 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
macOS Tahoe 26.4 mixed everyday app and accessory additions with charging controls, Network MIDI work, storage fixes, and an early compatibility warning about the eventual end of Rosetta.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately 18 topic areas and 24 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
tvOS 26.4 refined audio-format transitions and simplified the video-app surface while addressing asset delivery, networking, and commerce reliability.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately five topic areas and nine listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
visionOS 26.4 added accessory and spatial-audio improvements alongside remote-rendering and asset-delivery work, with several documented limitations that remained relevant to developers.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately seven topic areas and 14 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
watchOS 26.4 brought accessory and workout shortcuts together with fixes for Workout Buddy, health behavior, proxy traffic, StoreKit, and SwiftUI user activity.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately seven topic areas and eight listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
iOS 26.5 introduced a beta of end-to-end encryption for RCS on supported carriers, the Pride Luminance wallpaper, Maps recommendations, and a set of StoreKit improvements and fixes.
Apple’s shared developer notes contained approximately four topic areas and nine listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; RCS encryption availability was described as rolling out over time.
iPadOS 26.5 was a compact consumer update with the Pride Luminance wallpaper and Maps recommendations, accompanied by subscription-commerce and StoreKit testing work for developers.
Apple’s shared developer notes contained approximately four topic areas and nine listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.

macOS Tahoe 26.5 had sparse visible release notes, but added power-connected automatic startup for qualifying desktops and fixed enterprise enrollment, networking, certificate, display, and StoreKit problems.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately three topic areas and eight listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
tvOS 26.5 was presented to viewers as a performance and stability update, while Apple’s technical notes focused mostly on StoreKit subscription and testing behavior.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately three topic areas and eight listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
visionOS 26.5 was a maintenance and security release whose SDK-facing changes were concentrated in subscription commerce and StoreKit testing.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately three topic areas and eight listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
watchOS 26.5 added the Pride Luminance face and corrected dual-SIM messaging and workout-audio behavior, alongside StoreKit receipt, entitlement, and testing fixes.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately three topic areas and four listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
iOS 26.6 was an end-of-cycle maintenance release that prepared Spotlight for iOS 27 while fixing Health, Messages, Stickers, Object Capture, StoreKit, and security issues.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately five topic areas and six listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; the page title still reflected the release-candidate stage and may change.
iPadOS 26.6 was an end-of-cycle maintenance release that prepared Spotlight for iPadOS 27 while fixing Health, Messages, Stickers, Object Capture, StoreKit, and security issues.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately five topic areas and six listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; the page title still reflected the release-candidate stage and may change.

macOS Tahoe 26.6 was the final planned point release, combining Spotlight preparation with a storage-format deprecation and fixes spanning compatibility notices, Health, Messages, enterprise identity, managed apps, and security.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately four topic areas and four listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.

tvOS 26.6 was a narrow technical and security maintenance release. Apple’s consumer Apple TV update article had not added a 26.6 entry when this record was reviewed, so this summary is deliberately limited to the dedicated security record and developer notes.

Apple’s live developer notes contained two topic areas and two listed fixes when reviewed on July 29, 2026; that sparse record should not be interpreted as a complete list of user-visible or security work.
visionOS 26.6 was a maintenance release that prepared Spotlight for visionOS 27 and addressed HealthKit authorization and statistics, StoreKit testing, general reliability, and security.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately two topic areas and three listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.
watchOS 26.6 was a compact maintenance release centered on HealthKit authorization and statistics, StoreKit testing reliability, and security work.
Apple’s live developer notes contained approximately two topic areas and three listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026; those counts may change.

This record covers the active iPadOS 27 cycle through Beta 4. Apple’s version-level plans span Siri intelligence, onscreen Visual Intelligence, child-safety controls, performance, and interface refinements; they are not all changes introduced by Beta 4, and the new Siri experience was announced for later in 2026.

Apple’s live macOS 27 developer notes contained approximately 75 topic areas and 248 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026. The page changes during the beta cycle, so these counts and known-issue states are a dated snapshot.

Apple’s version-level plans include Siri intelligence, gaze access, spatial Mac workflows, richer environments, curved windows, and interface improvements; these are not all Beta 4 deltas, and the new Siri experience was announced for later in 2026.

Apple’s live visionOS 27 developer notes contained approximately 47 topic areas and 140 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026. The page changes during the beta cycle, so these counts and known-issue states are a dated snapshot.

This record covers the active watchOS 27 cycle through Beta 4. Apple’s version-level plans span Siri intelligence, interaction changes, workout assistance, indoor-distance improvements, and reproductive-health features; these are not all Beta 4 deltas, and the new Siri experience was announced for later in 2026.

Apple’s live watchOS 27 developer notes contained approximately 23 topic areas and 54 listed items when reviewed on July 29, 2026. The page changes during the beta cycle, so these counts and known-issue states are a dated snapshot.

events.summary: The public iOS 26 release established Apple’s new design language and expanded communication, assistance, CarPlay, and Wallet capabilities.

changes.title: Liquid Glass and screen personalization
changes.canonicalSummary: A translucent visual system and expanded Lock Screen and Home Screen controls changed the appearance and personalization model of iOS.
changes.summary: iOS 26 introduced Liquid Glass, an adaptive Lock Screen clock, spatial scenes, and additional icon appearances.

changes.title: Onscreen Visual Intelligence
changes.canonicalSummary: Visual Intelligence can analyze content already visible on the device and offer searches or actions related to that content.
changes.summary: The release expanded Visual Intelligence from the camera to onscreen content, with search and action options based on what is displayed.

changes.title: Live Translation across communication apps
changes.canonicalSummary: Live Translation adds language assistance to conversations across Messages, FaceTime, Phone, and supported AirPods experiences.
changes.summary: Messages, FaceTime, Phone, and supported AirPods gained translated conversation experiences, subject to device, language, and region requirements.

changes.title: Call Screening and Hold Assist
changes.canonicalSummary: Phone can gather context from unfamiliar callers and help users wait through a hold before returning them to the call.
changes.summary: Call Screening, Hold Assist, and new organization for calls from unknown numbers reduced interruptions and time spent waiting on hold.

changes.title: CarPlay communication and glanceable updates
changes.canonicalSummary: CarPlay gained a revised interface and richer communication and glanceable information while driving.
changes.summary: CarPlay added a refreshed interface, compact call presentation, widgets, Live Activities, Tapbacks, and pinned conversations.

changes.title: Wallet travel and order tools
changes.canonicalSummary: Wallet broadened boarding-pass, order-tracking, and payment options for supported issuers and merchants.
changes.summary: Wallet added richer boarding passes, expanded order tracking, and additional supported financing experiences, with availability varying by partner and region.

events.summary: The public iOS 26.4 release combined consumer features, accessibility work, accessory support, background-asset reliability, and stronger protection on newly configured devices.

changes.title: Playlist Playground and concert discovery
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music added a tool for creating playlists from prompts and new ways to discover nearby performances.
changes.summary: Playlist Playground supported prompt-guided playlist creation, while Concerts added artist and nearby-show discovery.

changes.title: Offline Music Recognition and Ambient Music widget
changes.canonicalSummary: Music Recognition gained offline use and Ambient Music became accessible from a dedicated widget.
changes.summary: The release added offline recognition history and an Ambient Music widget for faster access to supported listening modes.

changes.title: Expanded visual and caption accessibility controls
changes.canonicalSummary: New accessibility settings reduce visually disruptive effects and provide more control over captions and interface motion.
changes.summary: Reduce Bright Flashes, Liquid Glass motion adjustments, and caption controls expanded visual and media accessibility options.

changes.title: AirPods Max 2, emoji, Freeform, and Reminders additions
changes.canonicalSummary: The update combined accessory compatibility with new emoji and productivity features in Freeform and Reminders.
changes.summary: iOS 26.4 added AirPods Max 2 support, eight emoji, Freeform creation tools, and urgent Reminders behavior.

changes.title: Background Assets state and download reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Background Assets gained clearer local-availability information and corrected a crash during asset-pack downloads.
changes.summary: Developers could determine offline and latest local availability, and an asset-pack download crash was fixed.

changes.title: Automatic Stolen Device Protection on new setups
changes.canonicalSummary: Newly configured or restored iPhones enable Stolen Device Protection automatically as part of the security posture.
changes.summary: Stolen Device Protection became automatic on newly configured or restored devices, strengthening default protection against account and credential changes.

events.summary: The public iPadOS 26.4 release added Music, accessibility, accessory, Safari, creative, and background-asset improvements.

changes.title: Playlist Playground and concert discovery
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music added prompt-guided playlist creation and tools for finding artist performances and nearby concerts.
changes.summary: Playlist Playground and Concerts expanded playlist creation and live-music discovery on iPad.

changes.title: Expanded visual and caption accessibility controls
changes.canonicalSummary: New accessibility controls address bright flashes, interface motion, and caption presentation.
changes.summary: Reduce Bright Flashes, Liquid Glass motion adjustments, and expanded caption controls improved visual and media accessibility.

changes.title: AirPods Max 2 and new emoji support
changes.canonicalSummary: iPadOS added compatibility for AirPods Max 2 and eight additions to the emoji set.
changes.summary: The update added AirPods Max 2 support and eight new emoji.

changes.title: Compact Safari tabs and window indicator
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari refined tab presentation and made the presence of additional windows easier to see.
changes.summary: Compact tabs and an open-window indicator improved Safari navigation in iPad multitasking workflows.

changes.title: Freeform creation tools and urgent Reminders
changes.canonicalSummary: Freeform gained additional creation capabilities while Reminders added stronger treatment for urgent items.
changes.summary: New Freeform tools supported richer boards, and urgent Reminders gained more prominent behavior.

changes.title: Background Assets state and download reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Background Assets gained clearer local-availability information and corrected a crash during asset-pack downloads.
changes.summary: Developers could determine offline and latest local availability, and an asset-pack download crash was fixed.

events.summary: The public macOS Tahoe 26.4 release mixed app and accessory additions with charging, MIDI, compatibility, storage, and virtualization changes.

changes.title: Accessory, emoji, Safari, Freeform, and Reminders additions
changes.canonicalSummary: The release grouped AirPods compatibility and emoji additions with updates to Safari, Freeform, and Reminders.
changes.summary: macOS 26.4 added AirPods Max 2 support, eight emoji, and documented changes across Safari, Freeform, and Reminders.

changes.title: Configurable Mac charge limit
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported Apple silicon Macs can cap charging within an 80-to-100-percent range to suit usage patterns.
changes.summary: A configurable 80-to-100-percent charge limit became available on supported Apple silicon Macs.

changes.title: Network MIDI 2.0 support
changes.canonicalSummary: macOS expanded networked music-device communication with MIDI 2.0 capabilities.
changes.summary: Network MIDI 2.0 support expanded modern MIDI communication between compatible systems and devices.

changes.title: Rosetta retirement compatibility notice
changes.canonicalSummary: macOS began warning about future compatibility changes for software that still depends on Rosetta translation.
changes.summary: The system added a compatibility notice to prepare users and developers for Rosetta’s future retirement.

changes.title: External HFS volume automount fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A storage reliability fix restored expected automatic mounting for affected external HFS volumes.
changes.summary: External HFS volumes that could fail to mount automatically were corrected in macOS 26.4.

changes.title: Virtual-machine installation display fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A virtualization fix addressed black-screen failures during supported guest installation workflows.
changes.summary: The release corrected a black screen that could interrupt installation inside virtual machines.

events.summary: The public tvOS 26.4 release refined media behavior and addressed legacy apps, asset delivery, proxy traffic, and StoreKit reliability.

changes.title: Smoother Atmos and stereo transitions
changes.canonicalSummary: Audio handling was refined when content or playback moved between Dolby Atmos and stereo formats.
changes.summary: tvOS 26.4 improved transitions between Dolby Atmos and stereo playback states.

changes.title: Legacy iTunes video apps consolidated
changes.canonicalSummary: Separate legacy iTunes Movies and iTunes TV Shows applications were removed in favor of the consolidated TV experience.
changes.summary: The legacy iTunes Movies and TV Shows apps were removed, leaving their content and discovery workflows in the TV app.

changes.title: Background Assets offline-state reporting
changes.canonicalSummary: Background Assets can report whether content remains available locally when a device is offline.
changes.summary: Apps gained documented access to offline and current local-availability state for managed asset packs.

changes.title: Background asset download crash fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A crash affecting certain Background Assets download operations was corrected.
changes.summary: The release fixed a crash that could occur while an app downloaded an asset pack.

changes.title: PAC proxy traffic isolation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Network traffic no longer bypasses expected proxy behavior in the documented PAC configuration case.
changes.summary: A proxy auto-configuration issue that could allow traffic to escape the intended route was fixed.

changes.title: StoreKit purchase-intent reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: StoreKit corrected a documented failure in purchase-intent handling.
changes.summary: Purchase intents in supported StoreKit flows were corrected for more reliable transaction handling.

events.summary: The public visionOS 26.4 release combined accessory and spatial-audio additions with remote rendering, asset delivery, and documented input and view limitations.

changes.title: AirPods Max 2 and new emoji support
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS added accessory compatibility for AirPods Max 2 and eight additions to the emoji set.
changes.summary: The release added AirPods Max 2 support and eight new emoji.

changes.title: Faster Spatial Audio in familiar spaces
changes.canonicalSummary: Spatial Audio setup and response were improved when using the headset in previously mapped environments.
changes.summary: Spatial Audio became faster to establish in familiar spaces.

changes.title: CloudXR foveated streaming support
changes.canonicalSummary: NVIDIA CloudXR remote rendering gained support for foveated streaming on Apple Vision Pro.
changes.summary: The update documented foveated streaming support for NVIDIA CloudXR remote-rendering workflows.

changes.title: Remote-rendering signaling header fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A documented signaling-header issue affecting remote-rendering connections was corrected.
changes.summary: visionOS 26.4 corrected signaling-header behavior in the documented remote-rendering workflow.

changes.title: Background Assets state and reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Background Assets gained clearer local-state reporting and a fix for an asset-pack download crash.
changes.summary: Apps could inspect offline and current local availability, and a documented download crash was fixed.

changes.title: Documented input and managed-view limitations
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple documented known limitations involving headset input, distant interaction, and managed views.
changes.summary: The release notes retained known limitations for headset input, distant interaction, and managed-view scenarios rather than presenting them as resolved.

events.summary: The public watchOS 26.4 release added accessory and workout conveniences while fixing Workout Buddy, health, networking, StoreKit, and SwiftUI behavior.

changes.title: AirPods Max 2 and new emoji support
changes.canonicalSummary: watchOS added compatibility for AirPods Max 2 and eight additions to the emoji set.
changes.summary: The update added AirPods Max 2 support and eight new emoji.

changes.title: Start workouts from the workout icon
changes.canonicalSummary: A direct tap on the workout icon can begin a supported workout with fewer steps.
changes.summary: watchOS 26.4 added a shortcut for starting a workout by tapping its icon.

changes.title: Workout Buddy response-delay fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A documented delay affecting Workout Buddy guidance was reduced or removed.
changes.summary: The update fixed a delay that could affect Workout Buddy feedback during a workout.

changes.title: Movement-disorder health behavior correction
changes.canonicalSummary: Health behavior for the documented movement-disorder scenario was corrected.
changes.summary: watchOS 26.4 corrected a Health-related behavior affecting the documented movement-disorder case.

changes.title: PAC proxy traffic isolation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Network traffic no longer bypasses expected proxy behavior in the documented PAC configuration case.
changes.summary: A proxy auto-configuration issue that could route traffic outside the intended path was fixed.

changes.title: StoreKit and SwiftUI user-activity fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The release corrected documented issues in StoreKit and SwiftUI user-activity behavior.
changes.summary: StoreKit transaction behavior and SwiftUI user-activity handling received reliability fixes.

events.summary: The public iPadOS 26 release paired a redesigned interface with a new windowing model and broader productivity and communication tools.

changes.title: Liquid Glass interface
changes.canonicalSummary: iPadOS adopted Apple’s translucent visual system across system surfaces and applications.
changes.summary: Liquid Glass reshaped system controls, navigation, and app surfaces throughout iPadOS 26.

changes.title: Resizable windowing system
changes.canonicalSummary: A new windowing model enables freely resizable app windows with familiar controls, tiling, Exposé, and a menu bar.
changes.summary: Apps could be resized and arranged with window controls, tiling, Exposé, and a menu bar, substantially changing iPad multitasking.

changes.title: Files and default-app workflow upgrades
changes.canonicalSummary: Files gained richer controls and Dock integration while iPadOS widened user choice for default applications.
changes.summary: Files added new organization and customization options, folders could be placed in the Dock, and more app categories supported a chosen default.

changes.title: Local recording and background-task visibility
changes.canonicalSummary: iPadOS expanded audio-input and local-recording controls and gave long-running background tasks visible status.
changes.summary: The release added audio-input controls, local recording tools, and Live Activity visibility for supported background tasks.

changes.title: Preview, Journal, Games, and Phone on iPad
changes.canonicalSummary: Several Apple applications arrived on iPad or expanded its built-in productivity and communication set.
changes.summary: Preview, Journal, Games, and Phone broadened the set of built-in iPad applications and workflows.

changes.title: Live Translation and intelligent Shortcuts
changes.canonicalSummary: Communication translation and Apple Intelligence actions became available in supported iPad workflows.
changes.summary: Live Translation expanded communication tools, while Shortcuts added supported intelligence actions and model-assisted workflows.

events.summary: The public macOS Tahoe 26 release introduced a new visual system and concentrated on personalization, Spotlight, Shortcuts, communication, and Continuity.

changes.title: Liquid Glass on Mac
changes.canonicalSummary: macOS adopted Apple’s translucent visual language across system controls, navigation, and application surfaces.
changes.summary: Liquid Glass updated the appearance of macOS and its built-in applications.

changes.title: Folder and control personalization
changes.canonicalSummary: Users gained more appearance and layout control over folders, icons, widgets, Control Center, and the menu bar.
changes.summary: macOS Tahoe expanded visual choices for folders and icons and made system controls and menu-bar layouts more configurable.

changes.title: On-device communication translation
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported communication applications added translation features that process conversations on compatible devices.
changes.summary: Live Translation added supported translated conversations with hardware, language, and region requirements.

changes.title: Intelligent Shortcuts and automation triggers
changes.canonicalSummary: Shortcuts gained model-assisted actions and additional ways to launch automations from system events.
changes.summary: Shortcuts added intelligence actions, model choices, and automation triggers for supported workflows.

changes.title: Phone app and iPhone Live Activities
changes.canonicalSummary: Continuity expanded with the Phone app on Mac and live status from a nearby iPhone.
changes.summary: The Phone app arrived on Mac, and iPhone Live Activities could appear alongside existing iPhone Mirroring workflows.

changes.title: Spotlight actions and Quick Keys
changes.canonicalSummary: Spotlight became a broader launcher for applications, files, clipboard history, and direct actions.
changes.summary: Spotlight added richer search across apps and files, clipboard history, action execution, and Quick Keys.

events.summary: The public tvOS 26 release refreshed the television interface and added shared-room music, calling, profile, and AirPlay conveniences.

changes.title: Liquid Glass on supported Apple TV 4K models
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported Apple TV 4K hardware adopted Apple’s translucent visual treatment across the tvOS interface.
changes.summary: Liquid Glass refreshed navigation and system surfaces on supported Apple TV 4K models.

changes.title: Cinematic TV app presentation
changes.canonicalSummary: The TV app adopted a more cinematic browsing design centered on poster artwork.
changes.summary: The TV app introduced a poster-forward presentation intended to make browsing more visual.

changes.title: iPhone microphone for Apple Music Sing
changes.canonicalSummary: A compatible iPhone can serve as a microphone and social controller for Apple Music Sing sessions.
changes.summary: Supported iPhones could act as microphones while participants used a shared queue, reactions, and onscreen lyrics in Music Sing.

changes.title: FaceTime profiles and caption improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: FaceTime on Apple TV added profile-aware calling and richer identity and caption presentation.
changes.summary: FaceTime gained Contact Posters, expanded live-caption support, and profile-aware calling behavior.

changes.title: Wake-time profile selection
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple TV can prompt viewers to choose a profile when the device wakes.
changes.summary: A wake-time profile prompt made it easier for a shared household to enter the correct personalized experience.

changes.title: Default AirPlay speaker selection
changes.canonicalSummary: Users can choose an AirPlay-capable speaker as the default audio destination in supported setups.
changes.summary: tvOS expanded default-speaker choices to supported AirPlay audio devices.

events.summary: The public visionOS 26 release made spatial content more persistent and expanded immersive media, shared experiences, accessibility, and enterprise capabilities.

changes.title: Persistent spatial widgets
changes.canonicalSummary: Widgets can occupy persistent positions in a user’s space and present glanceable information in spatial layouts.
changes.summary: visionOS 26 introduced spatial widgets that remain placed in the environment across sessions.

changes.title: Spatial scenes from photos
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported photos can be transformed into scenes with spatial depth for viewing on Apple Vision Pro.
changes.summary: The Photos experience added spatial scenes that create a depth effect from supported images.

changes.title: Spatial web and immersive Safari content
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari and web technologies gained support for spatial layouts, 3D objects, and immersive media experiences.
changes.summary: Safari expanded web content into spatial and immersive presentations, including supported 3D and media experiences.

changes.title: Improved Personas and shared experiences
changes.canonicalSummary: Personas and shared spatial sessions received visual and interaction improvements for communication and collaboration.
changes.summary: Personas became more expressive and shared experiences gained additional ways for participants to interact together.

changes.title: Wide-field immersive media support
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS expanded support for 180-degree, 360-degree, and wide-field immersive video formats.
changes.summary: The release broadened playback and creation pathways for supported immersive and wide-field media.

changes.title: Spatial accessibility improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: New accessibility controls expanded how users navigate and interact with spatial applications and media.
changes.summary: visionOS 26 added documented accessibility improvements across viewing, navigation, and spatial interaction.

events.summary: The public watchOS 26 release paired a new visual system with health interpretation, workout assistance, proactive suggestions, and messaging upgrades.

changes.title: Liquid Glass on Apple Watch
changes.canonicalSummary: watchOS adopted Apple’s translucent visual system across system and application surfaces.
changes.summary: Liquid Glass refreshed controls, navigation, and supported app interfaces on Apple Watch.

changes.title: Hypertension notifications
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported Apple Watch models can identify patterns associated with possible chronic high blood pressure and notify eligible users.
changes.summary: Hypertension notifications added long-term pattern detection with age, device, region, and regulatory limits; Apple states that the feature is not a diagnosis.

changes.title: Sleep Score
changes.canonicalSummary: Sleep data can be summarized into a score intended to make nightly sleep patterns easier to interpret.
changes.summary: Sleep Score added a concise nightly measure derived from supported sleep information.

changes.title: Workout Buddy
changes.canonicalSummary: Workout Buddy uses supported Apple Intelligence capabilities to provide personalized spoken workout encouragement.
changes.summary: Workout Buddy added personalized encouragement during supported workouts, subject to device, language, and nearby-iPhone requirements.

changes.title: Smart Stack hints
changes.canonicalSummary: The Smart Stack can surface contextual visual hints when the system predicts a relevant widget or action.
changes.summary: Contextual hints made suggested Smart Stack content more proactive and visible.

changes.title: Messages communication upgrades
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages on Apple Watch gained additional conversation, translation, and response capabilities.
changes.summary: watchOS 26 expanded supported Messages interactions and communication assistance on Apple Watch.

events.summary: The public iOS 26.5 release added a carrier-dependent RCS encryption beta and smaller consumer additions alongside StoreKit work and wallpaper fixes.

changes.title: RCS end-to-end encryption beta
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported RCS conversations can use end-to-end encryption where participating carriers and devices meet Apple’s requirements.
changes.summary: iOS 26.5 began a beta rollout of RCS end-to-end encryption for supported carriers, with availability expanding over time.

changes.title: Pride Luminance wallpaper
changes.canonicalSummary: A Pride Luminance wallpaper adds a new animated visual option tied to Apple’s Pride collection.
changes.summary: The Pride Luminance wallpaper was added to the iPhone wallpaper gallery.

changes.title: Suggested Places in Maps
changes.canonicalSummary: Maps can surface place recommendations based on supported contextual and usage signals.
changes.summary: Suggested Places added recommendations intended to make destination discovery easier in Maps.

changes.title: StoreKit annual-commitment monthly plans
changes.canonicalSummary: StoreKit added support for subscription offers that pair an annual commitment with monthly billing.
changes.summary: Developers gained APIs for supported subscription plans with an annual commitment and monthly payments.

changes.title: StoreKit receipt and calendar fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: StoreKit corrected receipt-version handling and entitlement behavior with non-Gregorian calendars.

events.summary: This Beta 4 page separates Apple’s cumulative iOS 27 plans from two interface changes independently reported as Beta 4 deltas.

changes.title: Next-generation Siri intelligence
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple announced a more capable Siri with improved reasoning, personal context, and a dedicated experience, scheduled for later in 2026.
changes.summary: This is a version-level announced capability, not a Beta 4 delta; Apple says the next Siri experience is due later in 2026 and subject to availability requirements.

changes.title: Spatial Photos and intelligent editing tools
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos adds spatial reframing, extension, and cleanup tools for supported devices and content.
changes.summary: This version-level plan covers spatial photo reframing and supported extension and cleanup tools; it is not identified as first appearing in Beta 4.

changes.title: Expanded child and family controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Family controls add website approval, app-category time management, schedules, and additional sensitive-content protections.
changes.summary: Apple’s iOS 27 plan expands parent approval and scheduling controls and sensitive-content protections; these are cumulative version features, not Beta 4 deltas.

changes.title: Interface, core-app, and transfer performance work
changes.canonicalSummary: iOS 27 refines Liquid Glass and targets faster behavior in core applications, Photos, AirDrop, search, and networking.
changes.summary: The version-level release plan includes interface refinements and performance work across apps, media, transfer, search, and networking; it is not a Beta 4-only claim.

changes.title: TV app automatic download controls
changes.canonicalSummary: The TV app can automatically fetch upcoming episodes and remove watched downloads according to reported Beta 4 controls.
changes.summary: Two independent publications reported Beta 4 controls for fetching upcoming episodes and removing watched downloads; Apple’s developer notes did not enumerate the interface change.
changes.verificationMethod: Corroborated by two independent publications describing the same Beta 4 interface behavior; retained as a reported, non-Apple-documented change.

changes.title: Photos fill-display preference
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos gained a reported preference that changes whether images fill more of the available display.
changes.summary: Two independent publications reported a Photos fill-display preference in Beta 4; Apple’s developer notes did not enumerate the interface change.
changes.verificationMethod: Corroborated by two independent publications describing the same Beta 4 Photos setting; retained as a reported, non-Apple-documented change.
